findings_qualitative.value: Compact line emission in Class 0/I sources rotates perpendicular to outflows; DCN best traces disk-like structure

evidence.quote: DCN 3–2 emission seems to reliably trace the compact disk-like structures of the embedded sources, especially notable in Ser-emb 15.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN and C2H abundances positively correlated in Class II; HCN and C18O correlated in Class 0/I

evidence.quote: Statistically significant positive correlations are seen between the HCN and C$_2$H abundances in the Class II sources, and between the HCN and C$^{18}$O abundances in the Class 0/I sources.

claims.hypothesis: CO is depleted early in the disk lifetime
claims.experiment: C18O/H abundances across Class 0, I, II, with optical-depth benchmarks
claims.result: Class 0 consistent with ISM (tau=8), Class I ~10x depleted, Class II similar depletion
claims.finding: CO depletion occurs on ~0.5–1 Myr timescale, largely set in embedded stages

evidence.quote: In summary, our results are consistent with a scenario in which CO is depleted relative to ISM levels on a $\sim$0.5–1 Myr timescale.

claims.hypothesis: CO depletion enhances C2H and HCN formation
claims.experiment: Abundance correlations among C2H, HCN, C18O
claims.result: No anti-correlation of C18O with C2H or HCN
claims.finding: Gas already high C/O; further depletion may limit carbon supply

evidence.quote: We do not observe an anti-correlation in the abundances of C$^{18}$O with HCN or with C$_2$H.

claims.hypothesis: 15N fractionation of HCN evolves with stage
claims.experiment: HCN/HC15N vs Tbol across Class 0/I and Class II
claims.result: Ratio ~90–290 in Class 0/I, decreasing with Tbol; Class II ~80–150
claims.finding: Photodissociation-driven fractionation increases as the envelope clears

evidence.quote: HCN/HC$^{15}$N levels range from $\sim$90–290 in the Class 0/I sources and decrease with evolutionary stage

claims.hypothesis: Deuterium fractionation of HCN evolves with stage
claims.result: Flat ~50–90 in Class 0/I; slight decrease to young Class II, tentative increase >3 Myr
claims.finding: D fractionation temperature-driven, no strong trend in protostellar stage

evidence.quote: HCN/DCN ratios are quite consistent across the protostellar sources ($\sim$50–90)

claims.hypothesis: Ices sublimation affects HCN in protostellar cores
claims.experiment: Compare hot corino vs non-hot corino sources
claims.result: HCN isotopologue columns systematically higher in hot corino sources
claims.finding: HCN-C18O correlation likely from sublimation of infalling ices

evidence.quote: An ice contribution is supported by that the Serpens sources with hot corino emission (cite: Bergner2019c) have systematically higher column densities of all HCN isotopologues

why_this_method.value: DCN used to define extraction region because it most consistently traces compact disk-like emission

evidence.quote: DCN seems to most consistently trace compact disk-like emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Used H13CN rather than HCN for column densities in some Class II disks because HCN is optically thick; 13CO instead of CO

evidence.quote: we opt to solve for the HCN column density using H$^{13}$CN as a proxy since HCN suffers from optical depth effects

limitations_admitted.value: C18O optical depth is a major uncertainty; rare isotopologue needed

evidence.quote: We emphasize that the C$^{18}$O optical depth is a major uncertainty in assessing both the absolute C$^{18}$O/H abundances and the relative trends between evolutionary stages.

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample: two Class 0 and three Class I sources

evidence.quote: our sample contains just two Class 0 and three Class I sources

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution too low to identify Keplerian disks

evidence.quote: is not high enough to definitively identify the presence of Keplerian disks
